segments.text: There was no war in heaven. No warning either. One moment the gods were there, and the next they weren't. Eighteen centuries ago, give or take, the shrines went quiet, and the processions arrived at empty altars. Whatever the gods had been to the people who worshipped them, was now gone.

What followed took a little longer to arrive. Systems broke, in different ways, for different reasons we mostly still don't understand. The center of the continent fell inward into what's now called the Mire. Above Lastrago, the sky tore open in an event that came to be called the Mazur. Thirekhet had come down into Molakar to cool the desert into a sanctuary and got perhaps a third of the way through. Neither the ice nor the desert has given ground against the other in eighteen centuries.

Divine magic was the worst of it. It had been a tool, only useful the way a plough is, because something larger was pulling it. With the gods gone it went feral, and the survivors, who did not yet understand it had gone haywire, kept trying to use it.
The results were on the scale you'd expect.
